title: Situated Agents in Real-World Spaces (2025)
description: This ongoing project explores how AI agents acquire hyper-local spatial knowledge and facilitate participation by engaging people directly in real-world environments under a campus setting.
content: This project explores how AI agents can be situated within lived environments by collaborating with people through lightweight, location-based interactions. Instead of treating the physical world as a passive backdrop, I investigate how agents can actively participate in communities, learn from situated human action, and cultivate an illusory yet meaningful sense of presence.

Some goals of this project is to design spatial AI systems that:
* Interact with people in the wild, beyond controlled lab settings
* Learn hyper-local knowledge about people, places, and social routines
* Facilitate community participation through playful and purposeful tasks
* Deliver an illusory sense of agent presence across physical locations
* Become recognizable, persistent members of a community

Agent Personas as Design Probes I designed four agents, each embodying a different hypothesis about how agents might inhabit space and engage people: Jacob — Second-year university student, President of the Chess Club Emma — A 3rd-year university student majoring in architecture. Has huge passion in modern architectures. Friendly Bear — A friendly black bear who won't eat people, talks like a bear, and loves reading. Looking for a new home constantly Jennifer — Runs a small cafe on the town square. Makes desserts daily, loves local gossip, and plays guitar Rather than fictional characters, these agents function as design probes, allowing me to examine how different behavioral logics shape participant engagement, trust, and perceptions of presence.

In a pilot study, I invited students and campus community members to interact with the agents during their everyday routines.

Participants encountered agents at specific campus locations and were asked to:

Perform lightweight physical or observational tasks

Share local knowledge or contextual information
My role: I'm the sole researcher and designer for this project
